title: Renewal & Expansion check-in - Verdant Energy
summary: AE-led renewal check-in to confirm Verdant's interest in doubling dedicated capacity, adding an EU region, and extending contract for 12 months. SE outlined benchmarking approach and discussed SLA targets, security docs, and implementation timeline. Agreed next steps: pricing & draft amendment, SOC2/security packet, and SE-led technical deep dive for throughput tests.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-31 14:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood CSM), Michael Torres (Verdant), Rashmi Patel (Verdant), Evan Liu (Verdant), Sofia Gomez (Verdant)

Summary: Renewal and expansion check-in — Verdant wants to bump to 2x reserved capacity, add a second EU region for redundancy and data residency, and extend current contract by 12 months. Discussed pricing delta, expected traffic patterns, runbooks for failover, SOC2 and KMS questions, and setting up a performance benchmark next week.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — um we'll run about 30 to 40 minutes, just want to make sure we cover capacity, regions, and the contract extension. michael, want to kick us off with your priorities?
[00:18] Michael Torres: yeah thanks alex — quick background, our seasonal peaks have been creeping up, we saw a 60 percent increase last month, so we want to double reserved capacity and also put an EU region in to meet some residency needs.
[00:35] Rashmi Patel: and from a procurement angle we need pricing for the 2x commit, and we also need a 12-month amendment, not sure on exact start date yet.
[00:49] Alex Chen: got it, ok. priya i'll hand over to you for perf and infra details so we can scope the benchmark and timeline.
[00:56] Priya Kapoor: yeah thanks — so recommended path is: spin up equivalent dedicated pool in eu-west-1, mirror config, run our throughput tests with a representative traffic replay. we'll do steady-state and spike scenarios. quick q — evan, do you have current p95 latency targets?
[01:14] Evan Liu: we're targeting 250ms p95 for user-facing endpoints; internal batch jobs can tolerate higher. during peaks p95 drifted to 420ms.
[01:27] Priya Kapoor: okay that's helpful, we'll aim to validate 250ms p95 with the 2x reserved config and then adjust batching and cache settings. note: sometimes our transcription earlier mentioned KV cache as k-v cash in docs — oh sorry, lol, force of habit.
[01:45] Michael Torres: ha no worries. also security — rashmi, anything specific?
[01:51] Rashmi Patel: yes, SOC 2 is a must, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, KMS integration for keys, and SSO with SAML. are those supported in the private control plane?
[02:05] Jordan Mills: yep — support for KMS/HSM integrations is in our private plan and Dedicated can forward audit streams; we'll share the SOC 2 pack and our SIEM integration guide.
[02:18] Sofia Gomez: procurement will also want a draft amendment showing the 12-month extension and pricing tiers before legal reviews.
[02:26] Alex Chen: understood — i'll put together a pricing delta for 2x reserved and the EU region and the draft amendment.
[02:34] Priya Kapoor: on benchmarks — timeline wise, if we get sample traffic and auth tokens from evan by end of week, we can run initial tests next tuesday and share results within 3 business days.
[02:47] Evan Liu: i can share traffic profiles and a sanitized replay by EOD Friday. one note — we run heavy long-context prompts in two of our pipelines, make sure the benchmark covers 2k+ token sequences.
[03:02] Priya Kapoor: absolutely — we'll configure sequence lengths up to 4k to be safe, include KV cache warmup and cold-start scenarios.
[03:14] Michael Torres: on SLA, we want to see uptime >99.9 for critical endpoints. what does redwood guarantee on Dedicated?
[03:24] Alex Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers — 99.9 is our standard enterprise target; we can scope a formal SLA in the amendment. if they want 99.95 that moves into premium add-on — pricing delta we'll include.
[03:40] Rashmi Patel: ok, good. and data residency — EU region needs to be physically in eu-west, not just routing.
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: yep, we'll provision eu-west-1 dedicated pool for you, same model & quantization profile unless you want to test a lighter quant.
[03:57] Evan Liu: hmm, might wanna try a 4-bit quant on some non-critical workloads to save cost, but need to see quality impact.
[04:06] Priya Kapoor: we can include quality checks as part of the benchmark, A/B the quantized variant vs baseline.
[04:14] Michael Torres: on costs — rough numbers now would help; we don't need exact legal pricing but ballpark so leadership can sign off on demo budget.
[04:23] Alex Chen: sure — i'll send a ballpark today and a formal quote with amendment in 48 hours.
[04:29] Jordan Mills: and i'll attach the SOC 2, network diagrams, and our SIEM forwarding docs.
[04:35] Sofia Gomez: legal will expect contract language around data locality and audit rights.
[04:41] Alex Chen: understood — we'll include data locality clause and audit log retention.
[04:47] [05:00] (crosstalk) Evan Liu: one more technical: do you support private VPC peering for Dedicated?
[05:06] Priya Kapoor: yes vpc peering is supported; for private deployments we have a customer-managed networking option — we'll include the topology doc. sometimes the earlier doc calls it vpn peering but it's VPC peering, small transcription mismatch.
[05:22] Rashmi Patel: any downtime during migration/provisioning for the EU region?
[05:28] Priya Kapoor: no if we do a blue-green approach with traffic cutover we can avoid user-visible downtime; there may be brief sync windows for caches etc.
[05:37] Michael Torres: great. next i think we should schedule the SE deep-dive to go over benchmarks and auth specifics.
[05:45] Alex Chen: okay — propose Tue Apr 6 for the deep-dive?
[05:50] Evan Liu: that works for me.
[05:52] Rashmi Patel: works here too.
[05:54] Alex Chen: perfect. to recap: alex will send pricing + draft amendment, priya will prepare benchmark plan and run tests after evan provides traffic; jordan will send SOC2 and SIEM docs. we'll target the technical deep-dive Apr 6.
[06:07] Michael Torres: yep, thanks all.
[06:10] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — notes will be shared. end of call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mistranscribed acronyms (e.g., KV cache -> K-V cash), minor speaker label swaps in auto transcription.
